angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 2,984,553 km at 24.26 pc = 1.64 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Baines et al. (2023), AJ 166, 268, HD 112185: the Gaia DR2 (Gaia Collaboration 2018) parallax the radius was computed with (Table 2), 41.22 +/- 1.84 mas, inverted (https://doi.org/10.3847/1538-3881/ad08be): 24.26 +/- 1.083 pc; Gaia DR3 gives this source no parallax (a two-parameter solution)
radiusSource: Radius 4.29 +/- 0.21 solar radii from Baines et al. (2023), AJ 166, 268, HD 112185: radius 4.29 +0.19/-0.21 solar radii (Table 7), from the limb-darkened angular diameter 1.644 +/- 0.02 mas (NPOI, Table 5) and the Gaia DR2 (Gaia Collaboration 2018) parallax (https://doi.org/10.3847/1538-3881/ad08be): 2,984,553 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 8908 +/- 54 K from Baines et al. (2023), AJ 166, 268, HD 112185: effective temperature 8908 +/- 54 K (Table 7), from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux of the SED fit (https://doi.org/10.3847/1538-3881/ad08be). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Baines et al. (2023), AJ 166, 268, HD 112185: effective temperature 8908 +/- 54 K (Table 7), from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux of the SED fit (https://doi.org/10.3847/1538-3881/ad08be)
surfaceGravitySource: Baines et al. (2023), AJ 166, 268, HD 112185: log g 3.59, from McDonald et al. (2017), as the paper lists it beside the diameter (Table 5) (https://doi.org/10.3847/1538-3881/ad08be)
spectralTypeSource: SIMBAD, * eps UMa: spectral type A1III-IVpkB9 (2003AJ....126.2048G)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, * eps UMa: main object type a2*, alpha2 CVn Variable
projectedRotationSpeedSource: SIMBAD, * eps UMa: projected rotation speed 25 km/s, the measurement SIMBAD prefers (2005yCat.3244....0G)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's measured spectrum (Kharitonov, Tereshchenko & Knyazeva (1988), Spectrophotometric Catalogue of Stars (Alma-Ata), record 635) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
